name: INA105KU_2K5
title: INA105 precision unity-gain difference amplifier (INA105AM, BM, KP, KU)
summary: A difference amplifier on one die: a precision op amp plus four laser-trimmed 25 kΩ metal-film resistors, wired as a gain-of-1 difference stage with no outside parts, or rearranged into inverting, non-inverting, averaging, summing, gain-of-2 and gain-of-1/2 stages. The resistor network divides the inputs before the op amp, so on ±15 V supplies the inputs can swing ±20 V common mode. Grades: AM and BM in TO-99, KP in 8-pin PDIP and KU in 8-pin SOIC; BM has the tightest offset drift, PSRR and CMRR; AM and BM share the tighter offset and gain-error limits. The die comes from two fabrication flows (CSO: SHE with a bipolar op amp, CSO: RFB with a CMOS op amp) that differ in noise, slew rate and short-circuit current.
key_figures: 72 dB min (KP, KU), 80 dB (AM), 86 dB (BM); -40 °C to +125 °C
250 µV max (AM, BM); 500 µV max (KP, KU)
3 V/µs typ (CSO: SHE); 22 V/µs typ (CSO: RFB)
±5 V to ±18 V, or 10 V to 36 V single

circuits.title: Basic power-supply and signal connections
circuits.description: The plain difference connection: V2 goes to -In and V3 to +In, Sense joins Output, and Ref is grounded, so the output equals V3 minus V2 measured against ground. Each supply pin has a 1 µF capacitor to ground.

circuits.title: Offset adjustment
circuits.description: A 100 kΩ potentiometer across +15 V and -15 V feeds a small current through 499 kΩ into a 10 Ω resistor from Ref to ground, so the Ref pin moves a few hundred microvolts and that shift adds to the output. A second 10 Ω in series with the +In input balances the 10 Ω now sitting under Ref. Trim range is ±300 µV.
notes: Misprint: VO = V3 - V3 should read VO = V3 - V2.
Offset adjustment range: ±300 µV.

circuits.title: Precision difference amplifier
circuits.description: An INA105BM in its standard unity-gain difference connection: -In takes V2, +In takes V3, Sense is tied to Output and Ref to ground. The output is V3 - V2 with no external parts.
notes: VO = V3 - V2; gain error 0.005 %, CMR 100 dB, nonlinearity 0.0002 %.

circuits.title: Precision instrumentation amplifier
circuits.description: Two op amps buffer the inputs with gain set by R1 and the two R2 feedback resistors; the INA105 takes the difference of the two buffered signals and rejects their common-mode part. The output is (1 + 2R2/R1)(V2 - V1).

circuits.title: Precision unity-gain inverting amplifier
circuits.description: The signal enters -In while +In and Ref are both grounded, so the op amp's non-inverting input sits at ground and the two matched resistors give an exact gain of -1.
notes: VO = -V2; gain error 0.01 % max, nonlinearity 0.001 % max, gain drift 2 ppm/°C.

circuits.title: Precision unity-gain buffer
circuits.description: The input drives both +In and Ref, and -In, Sense and Output are tied together, so the output follows the input with gain 1.
notes: VO = V1; gain error 0.001 % max.

circuits.title: Precision average-value amplifier
circuits.description: Two signals enter at Ref and +In; the matched pair averages them at the op amp's non-inverting input, and with -In, Sense and Output joined the op amp follows that average.

circuits.title: Precision gain = 2 amplifier
circuits.description: The input drives +In and Ref together and -In is grounded; Sense to Output closes the loop for a non-inverting gain of 2 set by the matched pair.
notes: VO = 2 • V1; gain error 0.01 % max, gain drift 2 ppm/°C.

circuits.title: Precision summing amplifier
circuits.description: V1 at Ref and V3 at +In are averaged at the non-inverting node, and the grounded -In with Sense on Output gives a gain of 2, so the output is their sum.

circuits.title: Precision summing amplifier with gain
circuits.description: As the average-value amplifier, with -In and Sense tied together and fed from an external divider R2 (from the output) and R1 (to ground), which adds gain of (1 + R2/R1) to the average of V1 and V3.
notes: For G = 10: INA106.

circuits.title: Precision gain = 1/2 amplifier
circuits.description: The input at +In is halved by the matched pair to ground at Ref, and the op amp follows that node with -In, Sense and Output joined. A ±20 V input gives a ±10 V output.

circuits.title: Precision bipolar offsetting
circuits.description: The INA105 averages a -10 V to +10 V input at Ref with the 10 V output of a REF10 at +In, turning the bipolar signal into 0 V to +10 V (±2 ppm/°C) for a converter that takes only unipolar input.

parts.value: unipolar-input device: VFC320 (0-10kHz), VFC100 (0-FCLOCK/2), DAC80 (0-FS, 12 bits), DAC703 (0-FS, 16 bits) or XTR110 (4-20mA)

circuits.title: Window comparator with window-span and window-center inputs
circuits.description: Two INA105s turn a span and a centre voltage into the two limits of a 4115 window comparator: U1 makes centre - span for the lower limit, and U2 subtracts U1's output from twice the centre to make centre + span for the upper limit. The comparator flags VIN high, inside (GO) or low.
notes: U1 output: Window Center - Window Span (lower limit). U2 output: Window Center + Window Span (upper limit).

circuits.title: Digitally controlled gain of ±1 amplifier
circuits.description: A DG188 analog switch connects the joined +In and Ref pins either to the input or to ground while V1 always drives -In. Grounded, the part inverts; tied to the input, the output follows it.
notes: Logic In 0: VO = -V1. Logic In 1: VO = +V1.

circuits.title: Precision absolute-value buffer
circuits.description: V1 drives the non-inverting input of an OPA111. Its output feeds back to its inverting input and -In through D1 and 10 pF, and reaches the joined +In and Ref pins through D2, with R5 (2 kΩ) from there to ground. Sense and Output are joined, and the output is the absolute value of V1.

circuits.title: Differential output difference amplifier
circuits.description: Two INA105s take the same pair of inputs with the inputs swapped, so their outputs move in opposite directions and the difference between them is twice V2 - V1.

circuits.title: Instrumentation amplifier guard drive generator
circuits.description: A transducer reaches an INA101AG instrumentation amplifier through shielded cable. An INA105 wired as an average-value amplifier takes the two first-stage outputs of the INA101 (pins 8 and 9) and drives the cable shield with their mean. RG sets the INA101 gain, and 100 kΩ runs from the lower signal line to ground.
notes: INA101AG pins 6 and 7 are its offset adjust pins, left open; pin 14 is Common.

circuits.title: Precision summing instrumentation amplifier
circuits.description: U1 sums V1 and V2 (at +In and Ref, -In grounded) and passes the result to -In of U2, which sums V3 and V4 and subtracts U1's output, giving V3 + V4 - V1 - V2.
notes: VO = V3 + V4 - V1 - V2.

circuits.title: Boosting instrumentation amplifier common-mode range from ±5V to ±7.5V with 10V full-scale output
circuits.description: A three-op-amp instrumentation amplifier (gain 100, for example an INA101 or INA102) is followed by an INA105 wired for gain 2, for an overall gain of 200. With the gain split this way the common-mode range grows from ±5 V to ±7.5 V for a 10 V full-scale output.
notes: First stage: conventional instrumentation amplifier, A = 100. Second stage: INA105, A = 2.

circuits.title: ±10V precision voltage reference
circuits.description: A REF10 makes +10 V; the INA105, connected as a unity-gain inverter of that voltage, makes -10 V from it.

circuits.title: ±5V precision voltage reference
circuits.description: The REF10's 10 V sits between +5 V Out and -5 V Out. The INA105, +In and Ref grounded, inverts the top of the reference onto its ground pin, so the 10 V splits evenly about ground.

circuits.title: Pseudo-ground generator
circuits.description: On a single supply, +In goes to V+ and Ref to Common; with -In, Sense and Output joined, the output sits at half of V+.

circuits.title: Current receiver with compliance to rails
circuits.description: A 0 to 20 mA loop current flows through a 100 Ω, 1 % resistor to V-; a matching 100 Ω from V- to -In balances the inputs. The INA105 gives the 0 to 2 V drop as VO, referred to ground.

circuits.title: Precision voltage-to-current converter with differential inputs
circuits.description: The output current flows from Output through R to the load, and Ref sits on the load side of R; Sense connects through a second R. The internal resistors add a share of the current, so IO = (V1 - V2)(1/25k + 1/R).
notes: For R ≅ 200 Ω.

circuits.title: Differential input voltage-to-current converter for low IOUT
circuits.description: Output and Sense drive the load through R; an op amp follower takes the voltage at the load and drives Ref with it. IO = (V3 - V2)/R.

circuits.title: Isolating current source
circuits.description: As the differential voltage-to-current converter, with a P-channel JFET between the current-setting node and a grounded load. The FET's gate goes to ground.
notes: The gate can be returned to +VS - 5V.

circuits.title: Isolating current source with buffering amplifier for greater accuracy
circuits.description: The low-current converter with a P-channel JFET added between the sense node and the load; the follower drives Ref from the node between R and the FET. IO = (V3 - V2)/R.
notes: The gate can be returned to +VCC - 5V.

circuits.title: Precision voltage-controlled current source with buffered differential inputs and gain
circuits.description: Two op amps buffer the inputs with gain (1 + 2R2/R1) ahead of the INA105. The INA105 output drives the base of an NPN transistor whose collector runs from V+, raising the available current; 1 kΩ from base to emitter. The emitter current passes through R into the load, with Sense and Ref across the two R resistors.

circuits.title: Precision 4mA to 20mA current transmitter
circuits.description: An OPA27 scales the 0 to 10 V input (12.5 kΩ) and adds an offset from a REF10's 10 V (50 kΩ), with 1 kΩ feedback. Its output drives -In of the INA105, whose output sends the current through the 50.1 Ω pair into RLOAD, giving 4 mA to 20 mA out.
notes: 4 to 20 mA out through RLOAD.

circuits.title: Example schematic
circuits.description: The difference amplifier with each supply bypassed by 1 µF (C1 on V-, C2 on V+), Ref grounded and a load RL from the output to ground.

operation.text: One op amp and four 25 kΩ metal-film resistors trimmed on the die. Because the resistors are matched to one another and track over temperature, gain error, gain drift and CMRR are set by the network rather than by outside parts. Wiring the pins differently gives difference, inverting and non-inverting stages.

Parts are built in two flows, each named by its chip site origin. CSO: SHE uses a bipolar internal op amp, CSO: RFB a CMOS one. INA105KP and INA105KU/2K5 may come from either; INA105AM and INA105BM come only from SHE. Noise, slew rate and short-circuit current differ between the flows, and a design should work with both.

Gain error comes from the mismatch between the on-chip resistors, and gain drift from the small mismatch in their temperature coefficients. The matched, low-TC network drifts less than a difference amplifier built from discrete resistors.

The resistor network divides each input before it reaches the op amp, which both widens the common-mode range past the supplies and protects the op amp inputs. On ±15 V supplies the common-mode range is ±20 V. Without added protection an input may go 10 V beyond either supply, with input current under 1 mA.
There is one operating mode. Performance is specified at ±15 V; the part works from ±5 V to ±18 V with performance changing across that range. A single supply of 10 V to 36 V is also allowed.

The two inputs need nearly equal source impedances for good CMR: a 5 Ω mismatch brings a typical part down to about 80 dB. A known mismatch can be balanced with a resistor in series with the other input.

The output is measured against Ref (pin 1), usually grounded. Any voltage put on Ref adds to the output, which allows offset trimming. Whatever drives Ref should have under 10 Ω source impedance, or CMR suffers.
Pins 1 and 3 must not be swapped, nor pins 2 and 5. The resistors have the same nominal value, but each is trimmed for its ratio to its partner.

Each supply pin takes a low-ESR ceramic bypass capacitor (0.1 µF) to ground, placed as close to the part as possible, with the supply trace running through the capacitor before it reaches the pin. On a single supply one capacitor from V+ to ground is enough.

Keep the two input paths matched in source impedance and capacitance so common-mode signals do not become differential ones. Run input traces away from supply and output traces, and where they must cross, cross at right angles. Keep outside parts close and traces short. In the SOIC and PDIP layout, ground pours shield the input pairs, Ref has a low-impedance ground connection and the bypass capacitors sit at the IC.
The TO-99 case connects inside to V-; nothing should be connected to it.
The output survives a continuous short to VS / 2.
